item.title: Talkie: a 13B vintage language model from 1930
item.description:
📝 What would they ask you. Training larger vintage language models will allow us to uncover these scaling trends. While vintage models dramatically underperform models trained on web data (which includes code), we’ve found that they are slowly but steadily improving at this task with scale.
🔗 Read more: https://talkie-lm.com/introducing-talkie

item.title: Ted Nyman – High Performance Git
item.description:
📝 Git looks like a version-control tool. It starts with objects, refs, the index, and history traversal, then moves outward into packfiles, maintenance, sparse working trees, partial clone, transport, repository scale, diagnosis, configuration, and recovery. It is written for engineers who need Git to stay fast as repositories, histories, and teams get larger: build and CI engineers, monorepo owners, developer-experience teams, and the people who wind up debugging strange Git behavior when the easy explanations stop working.
🔗 Read more: https://gitperf.com/
